title: SquidRouterModule — attacker-chosen delegate in cross-chain payload drains Safe modules
closed_reasons: 59 traced 2026-05-25 Ethereum victims disabled the module (execTransactionFromModule reverts GS104)
the 34 still-enabled Safes hold only ~$2.10 gross combined (token dust + 0.0004388 ETH); net of gas is negative
the module contract itself holds 0 ETH and only 10 valueless spam tokens
NFTs are not movable through the module's fixed action set (swaps/approvals/wrap-unwrap only)
key_facts: module 0x1f1d37a3Bf840e35c6a860c7C2dA71Fe555123ca (verified, no proxy, no pause) is an Axelar express-executable Safe module

_processPayload() decodes (module, safe, delegate, actions) from an attacker-controlled bridged payload and trusts `delegate` for permissionsManager.hasPermission(safe, delegate, ...) with no signature or caller binding
expressExecuteWithToken() is externally callable by anyone with 1 wei of a gateway-mapped token and a fresh commandId — no bridge required
150 Safes ever enabled the module; 116 disable events; 34 Safes are enabled today (events replay + Safe Tx Service + live isModuleEnabled all agree)
all 34 still-enabled Safes have 1-2 delegates holding '*' for the module; permissions were never revoked
gross live balances of the 34: tokens ~$0.93 + 0.0004388 ETH (~$1.17) = ~$2.10 at 2026-10-03 prices; largest single item 0.00036 ETH ($0.96)
gas for a drain tx (~2-4M) is ~$27-215 at 5-20 gwei, i.e. far above the gross extractable -> net $0
supplementary same-address surface: Base 31 Safes enabled (~$0.37), Arbitrum 32 Safes enabled (~$0.09)
incident 2026-05-25: ~$3.2M-$4M from 86-88 Safes across Ethereum/Base/Arbitrum (Halborn/Common Prefix/Blockaid); 0 of the 59 Ethereum victims traced here remain enabled
the module is unrelated to Squid Router; the fixed sourceAddress string check in _executeWithToken is public and caller-suppliable
caveats: USD uses DefiLlama/Blockscout prices on 2026-10-03 (~$2,677/ETH, ~$84,530/WBTC); spam tokens unpriced
gross Ethereum total from the complete local computation is $2.10; the CI artifact estimate of $1.75 is a lower bound caused by price-API 429s during the CI run
extractable = ERC20 + native balances reachable via the module's action set; NFTs and arbitrary calls are not reachable
Base enabled-status is from Safe Tx Service + RPC (full event replay not run); Arbitrum likewise
the 88-victim count from public reporting spans three chains; only 59 Ethereum victims were traced from module events
read-only research; PoC runs on a local fork only, no mainnet transactions
one_liner: external unprivileged attacker can extract ~$0 net live (gross dust ~$2.10 across 34 still-enabled Safes): the drain path is fully open but every remaining Safe holds only dust and gas costs more; all real victims disabled the module
